title: Finite discrete fibre over a DVR point
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $x\in X$ have local ring $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For every generic point $\eta$ of every irreducible component of $Y$, assume the residue field extension $\kappa(f(\eta))\subseteq\kappa(\eta)$ is algebraic (every element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over the smaller field) [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-residue-field]. Then $R$ is Noetherian and normal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $f$ is quasi-finite at every point above $x$ [pqf-def-quasifinite], and the scheme fibre $Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ has finite discrete underlying space, identified with $f^{-1}(\{x\})$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre].

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof (2), and Tag 0AB7 (lemma-finite-in-codim-1), proof through quasi-finiteness (Tag 0AB6, lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1), discrete fibre and quasi-compactness, before the finite-near detour.

proof.text: By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $R$ is an integral domain and every ideal of $R$ is principal. Thus $R$ is a principal ideal domain. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] to obtain both that $R$ is Noetherian and that $R$ is normal.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr: the PID and normal-domain characterizations; Noetherianness of a principal ideal ring.

proof.text: Properness makes $f$ of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-generically-finite-quasifinite-over-dimension-one] with $(g,Z,S,s)=(f,Y,X,x)$. Its Noetherian stalk hypothesis is Step 1, its local dimension bound follows from the assumed $\dim R=1$, and its residue-field hypothesis is exactly the assumed algebraicity at every component generic point of $Y$. It follows that $f$ is quasi-finite at every $y$ with $f(y)=x$.

source.place: Tag 0AB7, lemma-finite-in-codim-1, first sentence of proof, applying Tag 0AB6, lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1, condition (1).

proof.text: Put $F=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. The first projection identifies its underlying space homeomorphically with $f^{-1}(\{x\})$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For every $y\in f^{-1}(\{x\})$, Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated] show that the corresponding singleton is open in $F$. Every subset of $F$ is a union of these open singletons. Thus $F$ is discrete.

source.place: Tag 0AB7, lemma-finite-in-codim-1, second sentence of proof; Morphisms Tag 01TH, lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, (1) implies (2).

proof.text: The structural projection $p:F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is the base change of $f$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. By clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], $p$ is proper, hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The base $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is affine by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Its entire space is an affine open, and its inverse image under $p$ is all of $F$. The definition of a quasi-compact morphism in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] therefore gives that $F$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0AB7, lemma-finite-in-codim-1, third sentence of proof; Morphisms Tag 01W4, lemma-base-change-proper.

proof.text: The open singletons of Step 3 cover $F$. Quasi-compactness from Step 4 gives a finite subcover $\{\{z_1\},\ldots,\{z_n\}\}$. Every point of $F$ equals one of the $z_i$, so its underlying space is finite. If $F$ is empty, take the empty subcover. Together with Steps 1--3 this gives all the stated conclusions, including the identification with $f^{-1}(\{x\})$.

source.place: Tag 0AB7, lemma-finite-in-codim-1, third sentence of proof: a quasi-compact discrete fibre is finite; the singleton-cover argument is written out.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0AB7, lemma-finite-in-codim-1, proof up to the finite discrete fibre, using Tag 0AB6; DVR ring properties supplied by Algebra Tag 00PD.
